context: The item is a second-hand phone, recently serviced.
transcript: Buyer ($60): A second-hand phone, even if 'recently serviced', is a huge risk and likely full of hidden defects. My absolute starting offer is 60, and if you don't take it, I'm walking away to find a seller who isn't trying to rip me off.

Seller ($190): Sixty dollars?! Are you out of your mind, or are you trying to rob me in broad daylight? I just spent good money servicing this flawless piece of tech, so give me 190 right now or keep walking!
Buyer ($80): You must be joking if you think a phone that already required repairs is worth $190. I'm taking a massive risk on this potential lemon, so $80 is my offer or I walk away right now.

Seller ($180): Eighty bucks?! You are spitting in my face with an offer like that for a freshly serviced machine! Look around, everyone wants this phone, so give me $180 right now or stop wasting my precious time!

Buyer ($100): Nobody else wants your refurbished junk, so stop pretending you have a line of buyers. $100 is my absolute limit for a phone that is one glitch away from the trash bin. Take it right now or I am walking away for good.

Seller ($170): Refurbished junk?! You're insane, this phone runs smoother than silk and you're insulting me with pocket change! $170 is my absolute final, rock-bottom ultimatum—take it right this second or get out of my face!
Buyer ($115): You're delusional if you think that repaired piece of junk is worth $170. I am stretching my absolute limits to offer $115, so take it now or I walk away for good.

Seller ($170): 115 dollars?! You are trying to ruin me while I stand here holding pure gold! I told you 170 is my rock-bottom, absolute minimum, and I'm not going a single cent lower. Take it for 170 right now or get lost!

Buyer ($125): You are delusional if you think anyone else will pay $170 for a phone that's already been opened up and repaired. My final, ultimate offer is $125, which is far more than this risky hardware is actually worth. Take it right now or I am walking away forever.

Seller ($170): 125 dollars?! You are bleeding me dry with these garbage offers! Walk away then, because $170 is my absolute final price and I'd rather smash this phone on the pavement than give it away to a cheapskate like you!
Buyer ($130): Go ahead and smash it then, because $130 is every single penny I will ever offer for an unreliable paperweight. Take this final $130 right now or I am walking away for good.
Seller ($170): Fine, walk then! You think 130 bucks is going to buy a pristine, freshly serviced phone like this? $170 is my absolute final price, or you can go buy a real paperweight somewhere else!

Buyer ($130): I told you $130 was my absolute maximum, and I am not paying a single penny more for a phone that's already been cracked open. Keep your overpriced junk at $170 if you want, but this is your last chance to take my $130 before I walk away forever.

Seller ($170): Are you deaf?! I said 170 is the absolute bottom, and you keep waving that pathetic 130 in my face! Get out of here with your cheap tricks, because 170 is the price right now or you leave empty-handed!

Buyer ($130): You are completely delusional if you think I'm going to pay $170 for a phone that's one glitch away from the trash. Enjoy holding onto your overpriced paperweight, because $130 is my absolute final offer and I'm walking away right now.

Seller ($170): Then start walking, you cheapskate! I would rather throw this freshly serviced masterpiece into the ocean than hand it over for a penny under 170! Don't come crawling back when you realize nobody else has a deal this good!
